NAME: ML‑IAP
TYPE: method

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Using the frozen‑framework approximation, where only a single Li ion moves while the host lattice remains fixed, reduces the generalization error of the ML‑IAP compared with fully relaxed MD or NEB simulations.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: The proposed descriptor‑based screening approach is not tied to a specific ML‑IAP; it can be employed with any universal interatomic potential model.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Finite‑size tests using a larger supercell and an ML‑IAP (SevenNet) show that diffusion coefficients converge within statistical uncertainties, confirming that the AIMD results are not significantly affected by supercell size.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Using an ML‑trained interatomic potential (ML‑IAP) enables validation of many more candidate structures than conventional AIMD, as demonstrated by MD simulations on 30 random and 100 top‑Ξ structures.
ARTICLE: Predicting ionic conductivity in solids from the machine-learned potential energy landscape

NAME: SevenNet
TYPE: cited_work
DIRECT_CLAIMS: Orb-v3 and SevenNet classify materials as good versus bad ionic conductors with accuracy greater than 82% using a 500 meV migration barrier threshold.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: SevenNet exhibits the highest fraction of good local geometry predictions (0.719) while MACE-MP-0 exhibits the lowest fraction of bad geometry predictions (0.190) among all tested MLIPs.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: MACE-MP-0 and SevenNet intermediate images provide better initial guesses relative to conventional interpolation techniques in over 71% of structures.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: Orb-v3 and SevenNet are suitable for high-throughput screening of candidate battery materials based on their >82% classification accuracy for ionic conductors.
ARTICLE: Predicting ionic conductivity in solids from the machine-learned potential energy landscape

NAME: M3GNet
TYPE: cited_work
DIRECT_CLAIMS: M3GNet and CHGNet exhibit systematic bias toward underestimating migration barriers, with 73.1% and 78.2% of predictions being underestimates respectively.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: CHGNet and M3GNet demonstrate superior performance for materials with low migration barriers but lack consistency over wider barrier ranges.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: M3GNet achieves test mean absolute errors of 35 meV/atom for energy, 72 meV/Angstrom for force, and 0.41 GPa for stress.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: MACE-MP0 performed best for discovering new stable materials with classification F1 score of 0.67, followed by CHGNet (0.61) and M3GNet (0.57).
ARTICLE: Predicting ionic conductivity in solids from the machine-learned potential energy landscape

NAME: CHGNet
TYPE: cited_work
DIRECT_CLAIMS: CHGNet achieves state-of-the-art performance on the Matbench Discovery benchmark, outperforming eight other submitted models.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: On the Materials Project Trajectory test set, CHGNet trained with magnetic moment labels attains mean absolute errors of 30 meV/atom for energy, 77 meV/Å for forces, 0.348 GPa for stress, and 0.032 µB for magnetic moments.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: CHGNet molecular dynamics simulations of Li superionic conductors reproduce room‑temperature ionic conductivities and activation energies within the error bars of AIMD, correctly distinguishing faster from slower conductors.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: CHGNet integrates magnetic moment labels as a proxy for atomic charge, enabling inference of atomic charges and accurate differentiation of oxidation states such as V³⁺/V⁴⁺ and Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺.
ARTICLE: Predicting ionic conductivity in solids from the machine-learned potential energy landscape

NAME: ab initio molecular dynamics
TYPE: method

DIRECT_CLAIMS: LiFlow achieves speed‑ups of up to ~600,000× over ab initio molecular dynamics (and ~400× over MLIP), predicting a 1 ns trajectory in 48 s for a 2 × 2 × 1 LGPS supercell and 352 s for a 4 × 4 × 4 supercell.
DIRECT_CLAIMS: The computational cost of LiFlow scales linearly with the number of atoms (O(n)), in contrast to the cubic scaling (O(n³)) of ab initio molecular dynamics.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: LiFlow trained on 25 ps ab initio molecular dynamics trajectories can generate stable trajectories up to 1 ns in larger (4 × 4 × 4) supercells, reproducing lithium self‑diffusivity, activation energies, and temperature dependence comparable to long AIMD simulations.
ARTICLE: Deep Potential Molecular Dynamics: a scalable model with the accuracy of quantum mechanics

NAME: M3GNet
TYPE: method

DIRECT_CLAIMS: The final M3GNet interatomic potential achieves test mean absolute errors of 0.035 eV/atom for energy, 0.072 eV/Å for forces, and 0.41 GPa for stresses on a held‑out Materials Project dataset covering 89 elements.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Relaxing test crystals with M3GNet reduces median volume error from 2.4 % to 0.6 % and energy mean absolute error from 0.169 eV/atom to 0.035 eV/atom relative to DFT‑relaxed references.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: A single‑CPU M3GNet relaxation completes in about 22 seconds, compared with 15 hours on 32 cores for DFT; pre‑relaxation with M3GNet shortens subsequent DFT relaxation time by roughly a factor of three and reduces total CPU time by an average factor of 2.97.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Screening 31.7 million hypothetical crystals with M3GNet identifies approximately 1.8 million candidates with predicted hull distances below 0.001 eV/atom, and among the 2,000 lowest‑energy candidates, 1,578 are confirmed stable (Ehull < 0.001 eV/atom) by DFT.
ARTICLE: Predicting ionic conductivity in solids from the machine-learned potential energy landscape
